exodus.17.p1.b1.text: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.

exodus.17.p1.b3.text: Why have you brought us out of Egypt—to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?

exodus.17.p1.b4.text: What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!

exodus.17.p2.b5.text: Walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.

exodus.17.p2.b6.text: And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.

exodus.17.p2.b7.text: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”

exodus.17.p3.b8.text: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.

exodus.17.p3.b9.text: Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.

exodus.17.p3.b10.text: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites,

exodus.17.p3.b11.text: while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

exodus.17.p4.b12.text: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed;

exodus.17.p4.b13.text: but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.

exodus.17.p4.b14.text: Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.

exodus.17.p5.b15.text: Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua,

exodus.17.p5.b16.text: And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.

exodus.17.p5.b17.text: The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.
